text_read: digest only; the 'How to Begin' passage is summarised by the search agent and only the exercises and attitude passages were confirmed in the digest
mode_evidence: She treats crystal pictures as externalised mental imagery: 'we shall find nothing in the crystal but what we ourselves put there', and every gazer she met was a strong visualiser. Her graduated exercises move from closed-eye visualisation to seeing the same picture in the crystal, which is a crossing of image into apparent outer space. No seen light as such is reported.
onset_evidence: Gives a graduated course for someone who sees nothing in the crystal: look at a room object, shut the eyes and visualise it, then try to see it in the crystal, expecting success after half a dozen tries if one has any visualising gift. She says that for non-visualisers the attempt is a waste of time. No light-specific onset.

conditions.gaze_or_eye_position: quiet gaze into a polished surface
conditions.setting: shady corner, guard against reflections (per search-agent summary, not confirmed in digest)
conditions.duration_and_schedule: repeat exercises again and again with increasing complexity
conditions.other: a flawless clean crystal if one wants to exclude reflection-seeded pictures

stages.label: graduated exercises (a) to (e)
stages.description: Visualise a room object with eyes shut then see it in the crystal; a recent scene; a described scene; an imagined scene; finally look to the crystal directly without prior visualisation.

what_to_do_with_light: Not about light; the picture is examined for memory, fancy or possible telepathic content.
obstacles_and_fixes: Fatigue or preoccupation yield only fancy and memory pictures: put the crystal away
Reflections can seed the picture: use a clean flawless crystal if that matters
cautions: Most crystal pictures are memory or fancy rather than psychical
Nonsense and commonplace pictures are as likely as significant ones
interpretation: The crystal is a convenient means of externalising images already in the mind, including unconsciously acquired knowledge.
practice_summary: Take a clean crystal or polished surface and guard against reflections. First train visualisation: look carefully at part of the room, shut your eyes and visualise it, then try to see it in the crystal. Move through a recently witnessed scene, a described scene and an imagined scene, increasing detail each time. When these work, look straight into the crystal without prior visualisation. Expect it to come easily after about half a dozen tries if you visualise well. If you do not make mental pictures of what you remember or read, she judges the attempt a waste of time. Put the crystal away when tired.

key_passages.paraphrase: Those who do not habitually picture what they think of will, in her experience, waste their time with the crystal.
